messages:
Maya: Quick sync - I want a concise, CI-friendly quality gate for new model bringups (including quantized candidates). Drafting a checklist, asking for pushes/simplifications.
Ben: Please make it machine-checkable where possible. Humans slow down releases.
Maya: Agreed. Proposal bones:
- canonical prompt set: prod_mix_v3 (stratified: short/long, qa/summarize/assist)
- baseline sample: 500 prompts default, with config to extend for low-delta detection
- metric matrix: EM for QA, ROUGE-L for summarization, BLEU where we still use it, and a repeat/ngram-repeat rate
- statistical rule: paired bootstrap (10k) for CI + p-value; fail if drop is statistically significant and exceeds absolute threshold
Aria: What thresholds? We need tiered tolerances by deployment target.
Maya: Right. My draft thresholds:
- "hosted": EM drop <= 0.4% absolute allowed, ROUGE-L drop <= 0.25 absolute, ngram-repeat <= +0.5%
- "dedicated/low-cost": EM <= 1.2% drop allowed if cost/latency gains >= 1.5x
- "experimental/private": relaxed, but must log and human-review
Josh: That seems reasonable. How do we quantify "cost/latency gains" for the trade-off rule?
Maya: Use measured p99 latency and token-cost estimate from runtime traces. We compute cost_ratio = baseline_cost / candidate_cost and latency_ratio similarly. Accept if cost_ratio >= threshold AND latency not worse than 1.2x.
Lina: For quant runs, add probes for token-distribution shift and repeated token degeneration. We've seen quantized models repeat more aggressively.
Maya: Noted. Add probes: token-shift KL, top-1 shift, and 4-gram repeat rate. Harness flags: `--probes token_shift,topk_shift,ngram_repeat`.
Ben: How about adversarial inputs? We should reserve a small curated slice of "stress_prompts" (30-40) that historically trigger hallucination or refusal regressions. Failing there should be a hard block for hosted.
Aria: +1. Also require a human spot-check when metric deltas are near threshold. Minimal human review: 12 samples across intents (4 intents x 3 each) with binary pass/fail and a short note.
Josh: Sample sizing note: 500 overall might not detect 0.5% EM deltas. We should include guidance in the intake form: short-run (500) for smoke; full-run (2.5k+) for release candidate.
Maya: I'll add that to the PR template. Also: bootstrap settings: `--bootstrap --n-resamples 10000 --paired` and seed recorded. EvalBot will upload artifacts.
EvalBot: auto: queued eval run: `./eval-harness --model=rwlt-6b-ptq --prompts=prod_mix_v3 --bootstrap --n-resamples=10000 --probes=token_shift,ngram_repeat`
Ben: Where do we keep the eval outputs and metadata? They need to be immutable artifacts linked to model metadata.
Maya: All harness outputs go to s3://redwood-model-intake/evals/{model_version}/{run_id}/ with a JSON manifest containing: commit, model_version, quant_config, hardware, promptset_tag. CI reads the manifest.
Lina: Also tag runs with `hardware` (e.g., a100-80gb), `jit-kernel` and `kv-cache` settings. Small kernel changes can change behavior.
Maya: Canary plan: if gate passes, rollout at 5% traffic for 24h with the following monitors: p99 latency, error-rate, sampled quality-check (hourly sampled prompts run in prod and compared), and infra errors. Auto-rollback if any cross thresholds.
Aria: For canaries: also run a short adversarial probe every hour (10 prompts) to detect sudden hallucination spikes.
Josh: CI enforcement: The intake PR should require a JSON artifact link and a pass/fail boolean. If fail -> block. If soft-fail -> require human review and an explicit signoff.
Maya: Soft-fail = metric drop within 0.1% of threshold or statistically significant but small absolute. Soft-fail must create a human-review task with 12 samples and a comment thread.
Ben: One more: keep a regression history per model family so we can spot recurring patterns. Store time-series of eval metrics in telemetry DB weekly.
EvalBot: note: run completed. Summary: EM delta -0.65% (95% CI [-1.0, -0.3], p=0.008), ROUGE-L delta -0.33 (95% CI [-0.5, -0.16]), ngram-repeat +0.9%, token_shift KL=0.015. Artifacts: s3://redwood-model-intake/evals/rwlt-6b-ptq/2026-10-05-12-03-22/manifest.json
Maya: This looks like a hard fail for hosted (EM > 0.4% and ngram-repeat > 0.5%). I'll stop the hosted rollout and open an investigation ticket.
Lina: Worth trying a different quant recipe and the disable-jit kernel variant. Also try kv-cache-preserve flags.
Josh: I'll update the intake checklist and add the CI gating steps + artifact validation.
Ben: Once Josh's PR lands, I'll wire the CI to block merges on hard-fail and add a soft-fail reviewer assignment.
Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll link the final checklist to the model intake template and run a follow-up eval after we try the new recipe.
Aria: Thanks. This should cut down surprise regressions. :raised_hands:
Maya: draft link: https://redwood.internal/confluence/eng-ml/model-quality-gates (will iterate)
_reserved_note: No title field per agents.md. Messages are a single continuous string with Slack-style short messages.
